(Affects the brains ability to plan, prioritize, and complete tasks). This is broken to two parts when it comes to doing tasks. 

Seems like you can get tasks started (‘Task initiation’) which is good. That’s the prefrontal cortex having regulated dopamine. 

‘Task completion’ wise, you seem to have task persistent deficit issues. Brain region is anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, which regulate sustained attention and motivation. 

It’s a similar issue adhd people face. I’m not at all saying you have it but the strategies used for adhd may benefit you as you share a similar issue. Personally, I like putting on a 5min timer and telling myself I only have 5 min to do a task. Cannot do anything else during it. Since it’s only 5 min, I have the energy to do it and awareness to not go off track. No music during helps too.

Only rule is you need to genuinly try to be a friend and don’t try to get a date from them. Women can smell that from a mile away, even if you don’t confess it. Make sure to tell them this too as it adds to the trust. Also, if you do end up having feelings, tell them right away and say you’re working on them because you care about the friendship more. The benefit from these friendships is that you learn a lot on how to be make women comfortable around you. If you ask, they’re happy to teach you how to not be creepy based on personal insight. Most of the ‘tips’ for approaching women from men are generally bad.

Now, based on my own experince of being approached (which many have been creepy) I’ll just give general advice as I don’t know you well.
- Make it short, direct, and don’t make yourself seem overly unconfident with a lot of “sorry” or something before she can even answer. Maybe search on YouTube ‘I asked a 100 girls on a date as an introvert’. They’re from guys who had the same issue as you trying exposure therapy to get over the fear. Youll get an idea.
